Summary view with SLOOS overlay:
- Policy stance: Cautiously hawkish. The FOMC held the funds rate at 4.25–4.50% and continued balance-sheet runoff, citing solid activity and a low, stable unemployment rate, but inflation remains above 2% and two‑sided risks have increased.
- SLOOS (April 2025) signal: Credit supply tightened and demand weakened. Banks tightened standards/terms notably for commercial real estate and for C&I at foreign/other banks (with large banks broadly unchanged), and reported weaker loan demand across C&I/CRE. Reasons cited include a weaker economic outlook, supervisory/legislative changes, industry-specific issues, and lower risk tolerance; some adjustments to credit lines were noted.
- Implications: The tightening in bank lending standards and softer loan demand point to additional headwinds for business investment and CRE, raising downside risks to growth and employment and likely easing inflation over time. This tempers the statement’s cautious hawkish tone and pulls the overall read closer to neutral/slightly dovish.

Net assessment: Resilient growth and elevated inflation keep a restrictive stance in place, but SLOOS‑indicated credit headwinds shift the balance modestly dovish versus a purely macro read.
